title: Break a Big Problem into Small Steps
subject: thinking

sections.body: Big problems can feel scary. A powerful trick is to break them into small steps. Programmers call this DECOMPOSITION.
Example: 'Plan a class party' becomes: pick a date, make a guest list, choose food, plan games, clean up.
Each small step is easier to solve. Then you put the pieces together.
In math word problems: 1) What do I know? 2) What am I asked? 3) What steps get me there? 4) Does my answer make sense?
Pick a goal (like tidying your room or building a model). Break it into at least 5 small steps.

quiz.q: Breaking a big problem into smaller parts is called…
hints: 'Compose' means put together. What word means take apart into pieces?
quiz.explain: Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller parts.

quiz.q: A shop sells 3 boxes, each with 12 pencils. 7 pencils are sold. How many are left? What's the FIRST step?
hints: What do you need to know before you can take any away?
First work out how many pencils there are in total.
Example: 2 bags with 10 sweets each, eat 4. Step 1: 2 × 10 = 20. Step 2: 20 − 4.
quiz.explain: First find the total (3 × 12 = 36). Then subtract the 7 sold: 29 are left.

quiz.q: Which is the best way to start a big school project?
options: List the small tasks and plan when to do each
Do it all the night before
Wait until you feel like it
hints: Which way makes a big job feel smaller?
Building a LEGO castle goes better if you sort the pieces and build one section at a time.
quiz.explain: Listing small tasks and planning them makes a big project manageable.
